evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep launches into logistics discussion immediately: 'Okay. So we can go about this two different ways. So first of all, I think the most, the easiest one is actually us picking up everything at the, excuse me, amo ranch house...' No time-box framing or promise of a dependable quote, no wait for customer confirmation.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves straight into logistics and pricing without ever asking 'what are your biggest concerns about this move, what do you want answers to on this call?'
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type not established clearly; floor/stories not asked; rooms count not explicitly asked; walking distance not asked; additional rooms/special considerations touched only via safe weight ($600 mentioned by customer, addressed by rep); no overflow/box count discussion.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Range provided (8.5–9.5 hrs for 3 movers/$2,731.50–$3,050; 6–7 hrs for 4 movers/$2,577–$2,989) but NOT personalized to customer's specific situation beyond mentioning trip fee ($105). No framing that ties the estimate to their stated concerns or prep level.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Trip fee disclosed ($105 outside 15-mile radius). No mention of 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, or 'not a guess' commitment. Partial credit only for fee transparency.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked 'Does that feel fair?' Customer concern ('I worry that they're wasting a lot of time in the truck driving over to the second house') is acknowledged and addressed, but the 'does that feel fair' close is absent.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No closure on the Two Promises section; no confirmation that concerns are addressed.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Call ends with 'thanks Justin. Bye.'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' Rep offers to email and lets customer decide: 'I can just email it all over and then you can have that way you can just look over everything.' Customer self-closes: 'I'll look out for your email and then I'll let you know...'
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Mentioned in passing ('We do have 8:39 AM arrival time for those dates available') but no explicit rate-lock or no-deposit framing per the script.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial: Date options discussed and confirmed (7th and 14th available). Arrival time mentioned (8:39 AM). Phone number and crew size discussed. But no explicit confirmation of addresses, no notes left for crew about customer concerns, no full booking confirmation sequence.

top_strength: Brianne navigated a two-location move logistics challenge clearly and provided transparent truck/crew options with honest cost comparison, helping the customer see the value of the four-mover solution.
coaching_note: Open with the quid pro quo framing (time-box and promise of a dependable quote) before diving into logistics, and never skip the explicit ask — 'Would you like our help with your move?' is the call-closing anchor; emailing an estimate without that ask leaves the close entirely to the customer.
